root_cause.text: In the GPIB NI USB driver, `ni_usb_init()` mishandled the failure path from `ni_usb_setup_init()` by returning an error without freeing the heap-allocated `writes` buffer, and `ni_usb_setup_init()` incorrectly returned `0` on internal failure, causing the init code to take the wrong error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `ni_usb_setup_init()` from `return 0;` to `return -EINVAL;` when `i > NUM_INIT_WRITES`, and in `ni_usb_init()` it adds `kfree(writes); return writes_len;` for `writes_len < 0` instead of falling through to `return -EFAULT`, directly confirming the leak came from the missing free in the error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the initialization routine to return an error when the write buffer would overflow.
intent_record.what: In ni_usb_setup_init(), the error path for i > NUM_INIT_WRITES was changed from returning 0 to returning -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: When the initialization write count exceeds the allowed buffer size, the function now reports an invalid-argument error instead of appearing to succeed with a zero return value, allowing callers to detect the failure correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ni_usb_init() to propagate setup errors correctly and clean up allocated memory on failure.
intent_record.what: The initialization code now checks whether ni_usb_setup_init() returned a negative value instead of only testing for nonzero. On error, it frees the allocated writes buffer and returns the error code directly. If no error is reported, it always calls ni_usb_write_registers(), then frees writes afterward. The old special case that returned -EFAULT when writes_len was zero was removed.
intent_record.how: This changes init-time error handling so that real setup failures from ni_usb_setup_init() are propagated correctly to the caller rather than being collapsed into -EFAULT. It also ensures the temporary writes buffer is freed on the error path, and it allows a zero-length setup result to proceed to the register-write call instead of being treated as an immediate fault.
